Focusing on the dynamics of the driving force of natural migrations; the seasonal movement of wild animals between pastures is a natural phenomenon but not everywhere.

We relocate two of the largest antelope species in Africa, the Kudu and the Waterbuck; both these species require a helicopter and very competent ground crew.

Classified as critically endangered, Black Rhinos are known for their unpredictable and aggressive behavior when approached or caught unaware; join the capture team in a capture exercise at the Hluhluwe-Imfolozi Park.
The red duiker thrives in the subtropical bushveld of the KwaZulu Natal province; this sensitive animal will be captured in nets, gently removed and sent on their way to a new home.
Traveling to the Entabeni Safari Conservancy where a family of African elephants awaits relocation; the family will be moved from a private conservation area as they have reached carrying capacity.

With a high reproduction rate that leads to large numbers on reserves and are the staple diet for predators that keep their numbers in check; seeing how these highly adapted and unique animals get loaded and gently treated to migrate to a new home.

Another member of Africa's Big Five, the white rhino; once on the brink of extinction, today thanks to the conservation and breeding strategies, there are enough to relocate to other nature reserves to ensure the survival of this unique species.
With helicopter blades turning precision flying and excellent planning, viewers are taken on an adrenaline-packed ride transporting wild animals including buffalo giraffe and warthog to new habitats.
When the animal to capture has a very long neck and standing almost five meters high and able to spot predators a mile away, the strategy needs to be dramatically adapted.

The capture team is busy in Ithala Game Reserve where several warthogs need new pastures; an interesting small animal called a "dassie" or rock hyrax is lured into traps as they are becoming a menace in the Ntshondwe camp area.
Being one of Africa's Big 5, the buffalo is an animal that requires a well-experienced team to capture and load; bushbuck on the other hand proves to be much easier to capture.
We've reached the end of the capture season; we attempt to relocate a black rhino cow and her calf simultaneously!

Only the strongest survive in the animal kingdom, where the competition for food, territory or mates means employing skillfully crafted tricks of the trade. "Animal Armory" incorporates high-end imagery and computer graphics to reveal how wildlife use their teeth, claws, antlers, camouflage, venom and even spit to threaten and intimidate rivals and predators alike. With weapons of deception, animals disarm and entice prey to their death. Meanwhile, perhaps the oldest weapons employed by animals are projectiles, which have evolved into their own versions of poison-tipped harpoons, chemical missiles and high-powered bullets.

Thankfully "Zoo Clues" fills in some of the blanks. Each half-hour episode investigates at least a dozen questions about animals to provide viewers with answers. Have you ever wondered if birds can fly backward, how animals without external ears hear, or why zebras have stripes? Those are among the questions waiting for answers on "Zoo Clues."
